events.description: Telephone call between the Secretary of State and President Musharraf, 1332-1338 EDT, on the response to the 9/11 attacks.
Terrorist attacks on the US including the World Trade Center bombing, attributed to Bin Ladin's organization.
Powell telephoned Musharraf (1332–1338 EDT) to discuss the terrorist attacks and Pakistani support; Musharraf pledged support and promised to review US proposals.
Deputy Secretary Armitage discussed a list of specific steps with General Mahmud, who responded positively.
Musharraf received Ambassador Chamberlin's credentials in a timely manner.
Terrorist attacks including the World Trade Center bombing killed Pakistanis among the victims.
Cable State 161371 transmitted the memorandum of conversation to the Ambassador.

key_claims: By 13 Sept 2001 the US had judged that Usama bin Ladin and his organization were involved in the 9/11 attacks, though not publicly announced.
The US considered Pakistan's unique relationship with the Taliban to give it a vital role in the response.
Musharraf pledged Pakistan would stand by the US in combating terrorism and support US proposals.
General Mahmud responded positively that Pakistan could work with the US on each item on a list of specific steps.
